idiom_name: ASP.NET Core gRPC service (Grpc.AspNetCore) with generated *Base overrides
implementation_notes: The .proto compiles into an abstract base type and message classes that act as transfer objects; the facade is the class overriding methods such as SayHello(HelloRequest, ServerCallContext) -> Task<HelloReply>, registered with MapGrpcService, while the client goes through a long-lived GrpcChannel and the generated client type. For a plain HTTP/JSON boundary the equivalent coarse facade is an ASP.NET Core endpoint or controller action returning DTO records, called through a typed HttpClient; the older [ServiceContract]/[OperationContract] WCF form is the legacy ancestor of the same idea. A hand-written proxy is still justified when the remote endpoint is fixed by a third party and no schema is available.
pitfalls: Service implementations are called concurrently; injected dependencies must be thread-safe (an EF Core DbContext is scoped, not shared).
Blocking on a Task inside a handler starves the thread pool, and every call must flow a deadline and CancellationToken from ServerCallContext.
Returning EF entities from the facade serialises lazy-loaded navigation properties and drags the persistence context onto the wire; map to DTOs instead.
